docs.title: Time-Based Analog-to-Digital Converter
docs.text:
Ongoing Work

This work is currently in progress.

While the architecture and design have been completed, the characterization phase is still ongoing. Additional simulations are required to fully evaluate the system performance.

Furthermore, post-silicon measurements have not yet been conducted, as the fabricated chip has not been received.

This documentation will be updated accordingly once experimental results become available.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This work presents the design and analysis of a Time-Based Analog-to-Digital Converter (TB-ADC) implemented in CMOS technology. The proposed architecture converts an analog input voltage into a time interval, which is subsequently digitized.

\[ V_{in} \rightarrow t_{delay} \rightarrow \text{Digital Code} \]

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
As CMOS technologies scale, voltage headroom decreases, making conventional voltage-domain ADCs less efficient. Time-based architectures offer an alternative by leveraging:

  • Digital-friendly scaling
  • Reduced analog complexity
  • High resolution through temporal quantization

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Voltage-to-Time conversion using a capacitive discharge mechanism
  • Delay-line based Time-to-Digital conversion
  • Thermometer encoding followed by digital processing

docs.title: Global Architecture
docs.text:
The system is composed of three main blocks:

  1. Voltage-to-Time Converter (VTC)
  2. Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC)
  3. Digital Encoding Logic

docs.title: About this Project
docs.text:
This documentation presents the design and analysis of a Time-Based ADC developed within a research-oriented context in analog and mixed-signal circuit design.

The project explores the conversion of analog signals into the time domain, leveraging scalable and CMOS-compatible architectures.

docs.title: Conversion Principle
docs.text:
The TB-ADC performs conversion in two stages:

  1. Analog-to-Time conversion
  2. Time-to-Digital quantization
\[ V_{in} \xrightarrow{\text{VTC}} t_{delay} \xrightarrow{\text{TDC}} D_{out} \]

docs.title: Signal Flow
docs.text:
• The input voltage is sampled
  • A delay proportional to the input is generated
  • This delay propagates through a delay line
  • A thermometer code is produced
  • The code is converted to binary

docs.title: Key Design Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Supply Voltage 1.8 V Threshold Voltage \(V_{thr}\) 0.5 V VTC Capacitance 1 pF Discharge Current 1 µA TDC Cells 255 Delay per Cell 5 ns

docs.title: Design Insight
docs.text: The architecture shifts complexity from the analog domain to the time domain, enabling better scalability and robustness in advanced CMOS nodes.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: This work demonstrates the feasibility of a Time-Based ADC using a VTC-TDC architecture.

docs.title: Key Achievements
docs.text:
• Linear voltage-to-time conversion
  • Efficient time quantization
  • Approximate 8-bit resolution

docs.title: Strengths
docs.text:
• Reduced analog complexity
  • Excellent scalability
  • Digital-friendly architecture

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Sensitivity to timing jitter
  • Need for calibration
  • PVT variations

docs.title: Future Work
docs.text:

  • INL/DNL characterization
  • Layout optimization

docs.title: VTC Characterization
docs.text:
Using estimated parameters:

\[ t_{delay} = 1\,\mu s/V \cdot (V_{in} - 0.5) \]

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
• Linear increase of delay with input voltage
  • Monotonic behavior
  • Good matching with theoretical model

docs.title: TDC Matching
docs.text:
The TDC range:

\[ 1.275\,\mu s \]

is compatible with the VTC delay span (~1.2 µs).

docs.title: Global Transfer Function
docs.text:
Combining VTC and TDC:

\[ N = \frac{t_{delay}}{t_{cell}} = \frac{C}{I \cdot t_{cell}} (V_{in} - V_{thr}) \]

docs.title: Gain
docs.text: \[ K = \frac{C}{I \cdot t_{cell}} = \frac{1\,\mu s/V}{5ns} = 200 \]

docs.title: Voltage Resolution
docs.text: \[ LSB_V = \frac{t_{cell}}{C/I} \] \[ LSB_V = \frac{5ns}{1\,\mu s/V} = 5mV \]

docs.title: Effective Resolution
docs.text: \[ N_{bits} = \log_2(255) \approx 8\,bits \]

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: The ADC behaves as a linear voltage-to-code converter.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Scalable architecture
  • Low analog complexity
  • High resolution potential

docs.title: Principle
docs.text: The TDC converts a time delay into a digital code using a delay line.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Chain of delay cells
  • START signal propagates
  • STOP signal samples the chain

docs.title: Time Quantization
docs.text: \[ t_{delay} = N \cdot t_{cell} \]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Number of cells: 255
  • Delay per cell: 5 ns

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: \[ t_{cell} = 5ns \]

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Delay mismatch
  • Process variation
  • Metastability

docs.title: Operating Principle
docs.text: The VTC converts an input voltage into a delay using a controlled discharge mechanism.

docs.title: VTC Simplified Architecture
docs.text: flowchart LR      %% ===== MAIN PATH =====     Vin([Vin]) --> SW[Sampling Switch]     SW --> CAP((VN))     CAP --> COMP{{Comparator}}     COMP --> BUF[Buffer Chain]     BUF --> OUT([vtc_out])      %% ===== ANALOG PART =====     CAP --> C0[C0]     C0 --> GND1[gnd]      CAP --> DIS[Discharge Current]     DIS --> GND2[gnd]      %% ===== THRESHOLD =====     Thr([Vthr]) --> COMP      %% ===== STYLE =====     classDef analog fill:#f8f9fa,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;     classDef digital fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1e88e5,stroke-width:1px;     classDef node fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#fb8c00,stroke-width:1px;      class Vin,OUT digital;     class SW,COMP,BUF digital;     class CAP node;     class C0,DIS analog;

docs.title: Sampling Phase
docs.text:
When the tracking signal is active:

\[ V_N = V_{in} \]

docs.title: Conversion Phase
docs.text:
Once the tracking phase ends, the capacitor discharges:

\[ \frac{dV_N}{dt} = -\frac{I}{C} \]

docs.title: Threshold Detection
docs.text:
The comparator triggers when:

\[ V_N(t) = V_{thr} \]

Solving:

\[ t_{delay} = \frac{C}{I} (V_{in} - V_{thr}) \]

docs.title: Key Result
docs.text: \[ t_{delay} \approx 1\,\mu s/V \cdot (V_{in} - 0.5) \]

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Higher input voltage → longer delay
  • Linear conversion behavior
  • Simple analog implementation

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Current non-idealities
  • Capacitor variation
  • Comparator offset
  • Noise and jitter
